title: Humach Retail: Sales Analytics
summary: Turn a compact sales table into defensible business evidence with aggregation, grain checks and visual reasoning.

tasks.q: How many rows are in the sales table?
tasks.hint: Count data rows, not the header.

tasks.q: What is total revenue across all rows?
What is revenue per order across the whole table?
tasks.hint: Total revenue divided by total orders.

tasks.q: Before joining another table, what should you confirm about this table?
options: The row grain and key uniqueness
tasks.hint: Joins are only safe when you understand what one row represents.

tasks.q: Write a two-sentence recommendation that cites at least one numerical result.
tasks.hint: State the evidence first, then the action.

title: Humach Retention: Customer Risk
summary: Frame a retention problem, define legal features and reason about validation, calibration and actionable interventions.

tasks.q: How many customer rows are present?
How many customers are labelled “At risk”?
tasks.hint: Count rows where segment is At risk.

tasks.q: What is mean spend across customers?
If multiple records per customer existed, which validation design would protect independence?
tasks.hint: Keep each entity in only one fold.

tasks.q: Describe one ethical limitation of using a retention-risk score to target customers.
tasks.hint: Consider proxies, unequal treatment, privacy or unintended harm.

title: Humach Energy: Demand Forecasting
summary: Use temporal structure, lag reasoning and legal forecasting validation to predict demand without peeking into the future.

tasks.q: How many hourly observations are in the dataset?
tasks.hint: There are two complete days of hourly observations.

tasks.q: What is the maximum demand (MW) in the dataset?
What is average renewable share (%)?
Which split is safest for a forecast?
tasks.hint: Future observations must not influence earlier training.

tasks.q: Name one lagged or rolling feature you would create and explain why.
tasks.hint: Use only information available before the forecast time.

title: Humach Health: Risk Screening
summary: Handle missing clinical values, prioritise sensitivity and reason about calibration in a screening setting.

tasks.q: How many BMI values are missing?
How many patients have risk=1?
For a skewed numeric feature with outliers, which simple imputation baseline is often safer than the mean?
tasks.hint: Choose a statistic less sensitive to extreme values.

tasks.q: For initial screening where missed positives are costly, which metric is especially important?
Explain why fitting an imputer on all patients before cross-validation is unsafe.
tasks.hint: Think about information crossing fold boundaries.

title: Humach Finance: Fraud Triage
summary: Work with rare-event detection, threshold trade-offs and cost-aware evaluation.

tasks.q: How many transactions are in the dataset?
How many transactions are labelled fraud?
What is the largest transaction amount?
For rare fraud, which evaluation view is often more informative than accuracy alone?
Describe the business trade-off in lowering the fraud threshold.
tasks.hint: More alerts catch more fraud but increase false positives/manual review.

title: Humach HR: Attrition Analysis
summary: Analyse attrition drivers while separating predictive association from causal or fair employment decisions.

tasks.q: How many employees are in the dataset?
How many employees have attrition=1?
What is mean satisfaction?
Which statement is safest?
options: Feature importance proves causal reason for leaving
Association can support investigation but not causal claims
tasks.hint: Prediction and causation are different questions.

tasks.q: Name one fairness or governance check before using attrition predictions operationally.
tasks.hint: Think protected groups, proxies, review and purpose limitation.

title: Humach Marketing: Campaign Efficiency
summary: Compare channels with cost-aware metrics and avoid confusing volume with efficiency.

tasks.q: How many campaigns are in the dataset?
What is total campaign spend?
Which channel has the highest aggregate ROAS in this miniature dataset?
tasks.hint: Aggregate revenue and spend by channel, then divide.

tasks.q: Which metric directly captures revenue earned per unit of spend?
Explain why the channel with most conversions may not be the best channel.
tasks.hint: Compare outcomes to the resources used.

title: Humach Mobility: Trip Demand
summary: Engineer temporal/weather features and reason about demand patterns without leaking future trip counts.

tasks.q: How many hourly records are provided?
How many records have rain=1?
What is mean trip demand?
Which feature is legal for forecasting the next hour if known in advance?
options: Next hour realised target copied from data
tasks.hint: Only information available at prediction time is legal.

tasks.q: Propose one cyclical time feature for hour-of-day.

title: Humach Manufacturing: Predictive Maintenance
summary: Detect early failure signals from sensors and reason about recall, false alarms and drift.

tasks.q: How many sensor rows are present?
How many rows are labelled failure_next_24h=1?
What is the maximum vibration value?
If vibration sensors are recalibrated, what should you monitor?
tasks.hint: Input distributions can shift even before labels arrive.

tasks.q: Describe one operational cost of false positives in predictive maintenance.
tasks.hint: Think unnecessary inspections, parts or downtime.

title: Humach Research: Repeated-Participant Study
summary: Design participant-safe validation for repeated measurements and recognise subject leakage.

tasks.q: How many observation rows are present?
How many unique subjects are present?
How many unique subjects have a positive label?
tasks.hint: Take one label per subject, then count positives.

tasks.q: Which split is appropriate?
tasks.hint: All nights from one participant stay together.

tasks.q: Explain why row-level random splitting can inflate performance here.
tasks.hint: The model can see highly related records from the same person in training.

title: Humach Vision: Image Classification Audit
summary: Audit image metadata, split integrity and class balance before training a vision model.

tasks.q: How many image metadata rows are provided?
How many images are in the test split?
How many images are labelled dog?
What is a dangerous split issue for near-duplicate images?
tasks.hint: Near duplicates can leak visual identity across splits.

tasks.q: Name one augmentation that could be reasonable and one that might change label semantics.
tasks.hint: Augmentation must preserve the class meaning.

title: Humach Graph: Node Classification
summary: Reason about graph structure, node features, message passing and leakage across connected data.

tasks.q: How many nodes are in the node table?
How many nodes have target=1?
What is mean node degree?
After two message-passing layers, a node representation can depend on approximately…
tasks.hint: Each layer expands the receptive field.

tasks.q: Describe one way a random node split can leak information in a graph setting.
tasks.hint: Training and test nodes may be directly connected or share structural information.
